channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Dani Lima: Campanha de Flávio assume desgaste e elo com ex-sócio de Vorcaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) campaign faces backlash after revelations that he returned from the US on a plane owned by Daniel Vorcaro and lawyer Willer Tomaz. Daniela Lima highlighted the negative impact of this connection with controversial figures on the 'Pulso Político' show.

item.title: PSOL pede investigação de Bia Kicis após investigado da PF fazer publicidade com nome Bia
item.description: The Socialism and Liberty Party (PSOL) requested the Supreme Federal Court to investigate an amendment of R$250,000 allocated by federal deputy Bia Kicis to the Viver-Brasil Institute, an entity linked to an individual investigated for ties to the film 'Dark Horse'. Kicis, running for the Senate under PL-DF, faces allegations of misuse of public funds.

item.title: Alckmin diz que Lula preservará tradições católicas em meio à polêmica sobre Nossa Senhora Aparecida
item.description: Vice-president Geraldo Alckmin stated that the Lula administration will protect Brazilian Catholic traditions amid controversy over an alleged initiative to remove the title of patron saint of Brazil from Our Lady of Aparecida. The controversy emerged after social media posts linked Flávio Bolsonaro to a bill archived in 2008, which he denied. Alckmin emphasized respect for all religions.

item.title: Boulos se licencia da Secretaria Geral para auxiliar campanha de Lula
item.description: Minister Guilherme Boulos (Psol-SP) will step away from the Secretariat-General of the Presidency to support Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's (PT) reelection campaign, with the role temporarily assumed by executive secretary Josué Augusto do Amaral Rocha. The leave, to be published in the Official Gazette on Monday (Sept 28), takes effect six days before the first round on Oct 4 and will be unpaid. Boulos had already been actively campaigning, attending public events and posting on social media, mirroring the strategy used by other government ministers like Luiz Marinho (PT-SP).

item.title: Felipe Roth detalha propostas de Renan Santos para a saúde
item.description: Felipe Roth, health coordinator for Renan Santos's campaign, detailed proposals such as SUS Fila Zero, prioritizing care by clinical severity, and the hub and spoke model for complex cases. He also discussed unlinking the constitutional floors for health and education from federal revenue through a PEC by Kim Kataguiri, and highlighted the absence of a childhood vaccination goal in the government plan.

item.title: Lucas Pavanato é condenado a indenizar a estudante da PUC por vídeo
item.description: Vereador Lucas Pavanato (PL-SP) was ordered to compensate a PUC-SP student for R$7,500 after sharing a video recorded without her consent during a university event in 2022. Judge Airtom Marquezini Júnior deemed the action unlawful following the revocation of consent for image use and mandated removal of the post. The ruling highlights ongoing debates around digital rights and personal data protection in Brazil.

item.title: Fachin manda PGR analisar pendências nos casos Master e INSS
item.description: Supreme Court President Edson Fachin ordered the Attorney General's Office (PGR) to review pending issues in the Master and INSS cases, assessing the relevance and impact of requested measures on ongoing investigations. The PGR has five days to submit an opinion, which will be sent to the STF. The decision follows the suspension of inquiries at the Presidency and the disclosure of messages between Moraes and the founder of Banco Master.

item.title: Lula enfim vai a Pernambuco pedir votos para João Campos
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) traveled to Pernambuco to publicly support João Campos (PSB), the candidate seeking re-election as state governor. The visit, which included First Lady Janja, marked a strategic alignment between national and local political leaders, reinforcing Campos' campaign with direct support from a key national figure. Polls show Campos in second place, just behind the incumbent governor, as both compete in an election seen as pivotal for regional political dynamics.

item.title: ‘Injustiça’, diz Deltan Dallagnol sobre proibição de fazer campanha mesmo com candidatura mantida
item.description: Deltan Dallagnol denounces what he calls an injustice regarding his Senate candidacy: his registration is upheld, yet he remains barred from campaigning following conflicting rulings by the Paraná Electoral Court and the Superior Electoral Court. He criticizes the judiciary for allegedly applying the law selectively against former Lava Jato members. Despite the ban, he claims his polling numbers have risen due to organic online support.

item.title: Fake news sobre Flávio e Nossa Senhora Aparecida circula entre católicos
item.description: False fake news circulated among Catholics claiming Flávio Bolsonaro intended to remove Our Lady of Aparecida's status as Brazil's patron saint. No such proposal exists from the candidate. The misinformation spread quickly through social media and WhatsApp groups.

item.title: Garotinho desmente rumores de que abandonou eleição no Rio
item.description: Former Rio de Janeiro governor Anthony Garotinho (Republicanos) denied rumors of withdrawing from the state gubernatorial race, stating in a live stream that 'he is a candidate and never considered quitting'. His candidacy registration was rejected by the Rio Electoral Court (TRE-RJ), and he awaits a ruling on appeals at the Supreme Electoral Court (TSE). The judicial outcome could significantly influence the direction of the state election.

item.title: Alckmin comenta polêmica envolvendo Nossa Senhora Aparecida e Flávio
item.description: Vice President Geraldo Alckmin (PSB) commented on a false controversy involving Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and an alleged removal of Our Lady of Aparecida's title as Brazil's patron saint. Alckmin stated that while President Lula is in office, religious traditions will be protected. Flávio strongly denied the accusations, calling them lies and attributing the campaign to the PT.

item.title: BH tem urnas para eleitor treinar voto antes das eleições; veja locais
item.description: The TRE-MG provides voting simulation booths in Belo Horizonte for citizens to practice before the October 4th election, with both in-person sessions and an online simulator available via the TSE website.

item.title: Medida de Lula contra bets é “hipócrita e eleitoreira”, diz Flávio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro accuses Lula of hypocrisy for banning online betting before elections, calling it populist and politically motivated. The measure will be announced in São Paulo, 10 days before the first round. Flávio promises to veto online casinos if elected but does not clarify his stance on sports betting platforms.

item.title: Lula proibir bets é 'desespero por votos' e pode ter impacto em eleição apertada, afirma professor da USP
item.description: President Lula announces the ban on online betting platforms ('bets') nine days before the first round, a measure with strong popular appeal (75% in favor) but whose electoral impact remains uncertain in a tight race against Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Lula promulga acordo de livre comércio entre Mercosul e EFTA
item.description: President Lula promulgated the free trade agreement between Mercosul and EFTA, effective October 2026, aiming to reduce trade barriers and expand market access. The treaty includes customs facilitation, investment rules and cooperation on intellectual property and sustainable development.

item.title: Pablo Marçal é condenado a pagar R$ 10 mil por soprar farinha no rosto de candidato em 2024
item.description: Former coach Pablo Marçal was ordered to pay R$10,000 in moral damages to candidate Marco Antonio Mills Martins after posting a video in which he throws flour in his face and associates him with drug use. The ruling was issued by the 1st Civil and Criminal Special Court of Barueri, based on a post that garnered over 7 million views.

item.title: Deltan diz ter sido “calado” no TSE por “indicado por Lula e melhor amigo de Moraes”
item.description: The Senate candidate from Paraná, Deltan Dallganol (Novo), claimed his campaign was suspended by TSE minister Floriano de Azevedo Marques, whom he accuses of being indicated by Lula and a friend of Moraes. He questions the impartiality of the judicial decision.

item.title: TJ-SP condena Pablo Marçal a pagar R$ 10 mil por danos morais a dirigente da Rede
item.description: The São Paulo State Court sentenced Pablo Marçal to pay R$ 10,000 in moral damages to Rede leader Marco Martins after the influencer sprinkled flour on his face and shared the video with derogatory captions online. The ruling, issued at first instance, emphasized the aggressive and defamatory nature of the act, which exceeded 7 million views. The decision can be appealed within 10 days.

item.title: Áudio: Estabilidade para grávida em contrato temporário vai a nova votação na CAS
item.description: The Senate's Social Affairs Committee is set to vote in a supplementary round on PL 3.522/2025, which establishes job stability for pregnant women under temporary contracts. The worker will be protected from pregnancy confirmation until five months after childbirth, based on decisions by the Supreme Federal Court and the Superior Labor Court. The text is expected to move forward as an advancement of rights for pregnant workers.

item.title: Lindbergh aciona STF contra Flávio e Willer por esquema na Loterj
item.description: Lindbergh Farias filed a petition with the STF requesting investigation into an alleged money laundering scheme involving Flávio Bolsonaro and Willer Tomaz at Loterj. The accusation indicates that Willer controlled RioPag through front companies, diverting over R$20.9 million in public funds.

item.title: TJ-SP barra 95% dos recursos destinados ao STJ e ao STF
item.description: The São Paulo State Court of Justice (TJ-SP) blocked 95% of appeals destined for the STJ and STF in 2025, preventing over 161,000 cases from reaching the higher courts. Only 6.5% of special and extraordinary appeals were admitted at the admissibility stage, according to the Anuário da Justiça São Paulo 2026 report. Despite this rigorous filtering, São Paulo led constitutional complaints filed with the STF, registering 481 cases in 2025, a 97% increase compared to 2021.

item.title: Como Nossa Senhora Aparecida entrou na disputa eleitoral e o que Flávio Bolsonaro tem a ver com isso
item.description: Bill 2.623/2007, filed by Victório Galli in 2007, proposed changing Our Lady of Aparecida's title as Brazil's patron saint, but was shelved in 2008. The controversy was revived on social media and linked to presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, who has been accused of supporting the measure, especially after remarks about the country's spiritual identity. The debate gains momentum in an electoral context marked by the growing role of religion in Brazilian politics.

item.title: A nova pesquisa Quaest sobre a eleição presidencial, a 6 dias do 1º turno
item.description: Polling institute Quaest will release a new presidential vote intention survey on Monday, six days before the first round. The survey, based on 2,004 interviews with a two percentage point margin of error, shows Lula (PT) leading with 37% against Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) at 33%. In a projected runoff, there is a technical tie with a slight lead for Lula.

item.title: Entenda a polêmica envolvendo Flávio Bolsonaro e Nossa Senhora Aparecida
item.description: GloboNews issued an apology and correction for a segment on its show 'Em Pauta' that helped spread the claim that Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) supported a bill to remove Our Lady of Aparecida as Brazil's patron saint.

item.title: Rayan salva empate para Brasil contra Austrália e Ancelotti pede paciência
item.description: A last-minute header goal by Rayan secured a 1-1 draw between Brazil and Australia in a friendly match. The game marked the return of the Selection under Carlo Ancelotti following the disappointment at the 2026 World Cup.

item.title: Eleições 2026: saiba a ordem de votação
item.description: In the general elections on October 4th, voters will make six selections on the electronic ballot box in this order: federal deputy, state or district deputy, two votes for the Federal Senate, governor, and president of the Republic. Voting takes place from 8am to 5pm, with the right to vote guaranteed for those in line at closing time. The machine displays the candidate's photo, full name, office, and party, with a one-second security pause before confirming the vote.

item.title: Os chocolates suíços vêm aí: acordo do Mersocul com o Efta começa a valer no Brasil
item.description: President Lula signed the Free Trade Agreement between Mercosul and EFTA, a Swiss-Icelandic bloc comprising Switzerland, Norway, Liechtenstein, and Iceland, effective October 1st. The agreement eliminates or reduces tariffs on bilateral trade worth $7.8 billion annually, benefiting sectors like chocolates, watches, medicines, and fertilizers.

item.title: Celina diz que apoio do PSD seria "aliança natural" após TSE barrar Arruda
item.description: Following the TSE's decision to block José Roberto Arruda's candidacy, Governor Celina Leão (PP) called a potential alliance with the PSD a 'natural' move, citing ideological alignment with the right. The PSD has not yet officially defined its support, stating it will decide after consulting party members and legislative candidates. The Avante has already endorsed Celina Leão's reelection bid.

item.title: AGU e Gilmar Mendes fecham cerco contra 'indústria de precatórios' usada pelo Master
item.description: The AGU and Minister Gilmar Mendes are closing in on an alleged precatório industry used by Banco Master to generate profits, based on data from Daniel Vorcaro's phone. Vorcaro allegedly contacted lawyers and judges to validate precatórios, with partial support in the STF, but Gilmar voted against. The AGU secured a ruling to block R$ 4.7 billion and the CMN tightened rules for purchasing judicial debts.

item.title: “GloboNews” corrige fala sobre Flávio e padroeira e pede desculpas
item.description: GloboNews corrected false reports linking Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to a bill proposing to remove Nossa Senhora Aparecida's title as Brazil's patron saint. The bill was filed in 2007 and archived in 2008, with no connection to the candidate. The network apologized for the mistake.

item.title: Lula intensifica populismo após acionar modo desespero na eleição
item.description: Less than two weeks before the first round, Lula's administration activated 'desperation mode', unveiling measures directly impacting income, prices, health, and even online betting regulation, aiming to counter Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) rising poll numbers. The intensified campaign seeks to reverse the trend of convergence between the two leading candidates and bolster Lula’s populist appeal ahead of the election.

item.title: Pacote de Lula contra bets prevê proibição e até oito anos de prisão
item.description: President Lula announced a ban on online betting and gaming in Brazil, using a temporary decree to halt operations and a bill that criminalizes operators, content creators and sponsors with penalties of 2 to 8 years in prison. The package aims to curb the growth of the illegal market and restrict advertising and player recruitment channels.

item.title: Lei transforma Cefets de Minas e do RJ em universidades federais
item.description: Law 15.521/26 converts the Cefets of Minas Gerais and Rio de Janeiro into federal universities, increasing institutional autonomy while preserving technical education. Signed by President Lula, the law establishes the Federal University of Science and Innovation of Minas Gerais and the Federal University of Science and Innovation of Rio de Janeiro.

item.title: O racha do PSD do DF sobre o que fazer após Arruda ter candidatura barrada pelo TSE
item.description: The PSD in the Federal District is divided after the TSE blocked José Roberto Arruda's candidacy, with Paulo Octávio's faction supporting Celina and Arruda's allies considering an alliance with Leandro Grass. The ruling has caused internal tension within the party, while the PT avoids public criticism of the former governor and seeks his support for Grass.

item.title: Governo Lula deve propor pena de até 6 anos de prisão para quem explorar ou operar bets no Brasil
item.description: President Lula's administration proposes a bill criminalizing sports betting in Brazil, with up to six years in prison and fines for operators, regardless of foreign licenses. The measure also targets advertisers and promoters of betting platforms, aligning with efforts to reduce household debt. The bill is set to be unveiled on Friday, ahead of the first round of the 2026 elections.

item.title: O estado em que Lula e Flávio empatam no 1º turno, mas senador vence no 2º, segundo pesquisa
item.description: A Real Time Big Data poll in Tocantins shows a technical tie between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round (40% each), with the senator projected to win in the second round (48% vs 40%). Both candidates have identical rejection rates of 48%, according to a survey of 1,600 voters with a margin of error of two percentage points.

item.title: Flávio prepara ofensiva na reta final e mira mudança de discurso de Lula
item.description: Flavito Bolsonaro prepares campaign to question Lula's shift on online betting, highlighting that the government regulated the sector in Congress. The strategy aims to expose contradictions and bring the prohibition MP into the electoral debate.

item.title: Lula quer acabar com as bets, mas arrecadou R$ 19 bi com apostas online
item.description: President Lula intends to issue a Provisional Measure to ban online sports betting, but the action will be taken a day before elections, after the government collected nearly R$19 billion in taxes from the sector. The decision has drawn criticism for appearing politically motivated.

item.title: Boulos pede licença não remunerada para se dedicar à campanha de Lula
item.description: Guilherme Boulos, Minister of the General Secretariat of the Presidency, requested an unpaid leave to dedicated himself to Lula's reelection campaign. The decision was announced on September 25, 2026.

item.title: Entre Lula e Flávio, Brasil dá as ‘costas para o futuro’, diz The Economist
item.description: The British magazine The Economist published an editorial stating that Brazil risks turning its back on the future in a new presidential race between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and the Bolsonaro family. The publication describes the two main candidates as 'depressing' options, highlighting that neither is capable of addressing entrenched corruption and the relentless increase in public spending. The magazine also questions Lula's age and Flávio Bolsonaro's positions on climate change and electronic voting.

item.title: Flávio tem 48% contra 40% de Lula no TO no 2º turno, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Tocantins survey shows Flávio Bolsonaro leading Lula 48% to 40% in a hypothetical runoff, with both tied at 40% in the first round. Lula's administration holds a 53% disapproval rating, while 48% approve. The poll, with a ±2-point margin of error and 95% confidence, interviewed 1,600 voters between September 21–24, 2026.

item.title: Meio-Dia em Brasília: O amor de Alcolumbre por Vorcaro; Lula aposta no fim das bets
item.description: The Meio-Dia em Brasília program discusses the exchange of messages between the President of the Congress, Davi Alcolumbre, and the former banker Daniel Vorcaro, highlighting mutual love declarations between the two. It also covers President Lula's new strategy to reverse the trend of supporting gambling in Brazil.

item.title: Crusoé: Economist endossa Renan e alerta que Brasil “vira as costas” para o futuro
item.description: The Economist magazine endorsed Renan Santos (Mission) as the candidate whose ideas best align with Brazil's current moment, warning that the country is 'turning its back' on the future. The analysis highlights Santos' libertarian positioning as an appropriate alternative to the electoral scenario. The article was published in O Antagonista.

item.title: Flávio tem 48% e Lula, 41%, no 2º turno no ES, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Real Time Big Data poll for Espírito Santo shows Flávio Bolsonaro at 48% and Lula at 41% in a simulated runoff. In the first-round scenario, Flávio leads with 39% versus Lula's 37%. The margin of error is plus or minus 2 percentage points.

item.title: Silêncio de Toffoli desperta desprezo de Lula e fortalece Mendonça
item.description: A Supreme Court justice's silence sparked public disdain from President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, shifting power dynamics within the court and escalating a crisis amid the 2026 electoral campaign.

item.title: Aliados de Flávio projetam 1º turno acima do estimado por pesquisas
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) allies project a first-round turnaround, placing him ahead of Lula (PT), contrary to polls showing a technical tie. Datafolha recorded 40% for Lula and 36% for Flávio.

item.title: Deltan será candidato ao Senado ou não? Entenda caso na Justiça Eleitoral
item.description: Deltan Dallagnol's Senate candidacy for Paraná is approved by TRE-PR, but he awaits a TSE decision on his ineligibility following the annulment of his federal term in 2023. He is currently barred from campaigning.

item.title: Pesquisa Datafolha mostra distância entre candidatos aos governos nos três maiores colégios eleitorais do país
item.description: The Datafolha poll released on September 24 shows Tarcísio de Freitas leading the São Paulo gubernatorial race with 50% of voting intentions, followed by Fernando Haddad at 30%. In Minas Gerais, Cleitinho Azevedo leads with 40%, holding a 25-point advantage over Patrus Ananias, who received 15%.

item.title: Saiba como estão Lula e Flávio nas pesquisas a 9 dias da eleição
item.description: Nine days before the first round of the 2026 elections, the latest national polls show a tight race between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), with the senator leading in five surveys and the former president ahead in four others. The percentage gaps between the two candidates range from 0.3 to 7 percentage points, accounting for the polls' margins of error.
